title: Partial, variable gap-junction blockade is consistent with stochastic head-shape outcomes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Partial, variable gap-junction blockade is consistent with stochastic head-shape outcomes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The variability and overall magnitude of the bioelectric effect imply that octanol only partially shuts down gap junction communication in each G. dorotocephala (affecting some percentage of gap junctions per animal), which the authors consider consistent with the stochasticity of the head-shape phenotype.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.4. Bioelectric State of Tissues and Its Stable Alteration in Species-Specific Shape Change

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The variability and overall magnitude of the effect imply that the result of 8-OH exposure is only partially effective in shutting down GJC (affecting some percentage of GJs in any animal); this is consistent with the stochasticity of the morphological phenotype (Figure 3).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “3. Discussion › 3.4. Bioelectric State of Tissues and Its Stable Alteration in Species-Specific Shape Change”. Scope: Octanol-treated G. dorotocephala

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.46

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Published voltage and phenotype variability are consistent with the claim but weakly discriminating. Direct per-animal coupling measurements paired with outcomes are absent, so only the indirect implication can be assessed.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure gap-junction conductance or tracer coupling per animal after octanol and relate the fractional reduction to subsequent head-shape outcome. A broad partial-blockade distribution predictive of phenotype would support the inference.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Existing data do not directly quantify the fraction of blocked junctions.

Variability can arise from pharmacokinetics, anatomy, or off-target effects.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.65
discriminating power: 0.3
data adequacy: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Partial effectiveness is inferred from variability and then said to agree with morphological stochasticity. Because the blocked fraction is not measured, every spread of outcomes fits the statement and also fits injury, dose, or expression noise. The agreement has no distinguishing observation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The sentence infers partial gap-junction shutdown from the variability of the voltage effect and treats that partial shutdown as agreeing with stochastic head shapes. Any stochastic outcome is compatible with some unknown fraction of junctions blocked and with other noise sources.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No fraction of blocked junctions is stated as a quantity that would refute the inference.

Shape noise and voltage noise can arise independently of partial blockade.
